# Generated by kiln 0.1.0 from .rn-forge/kiln/config.toml — do not edit; run 'kiln apply'

# The repository standard — ngkit

This is `docs/reference/standard-repo.md` from the kiln repo, rendered with this
repo's archetype, docs profile and task surface filled in. It is the normative
text for anyone — human or agent — working here. The reasoning behind each rule
is a kiln ADR; this file states the rule.

- **Archetype:** `node-lib` — a pnpm-managed Nx workspace of Angular libraries,
  one release group, with no projects until the repository adds them; docs
  tooling through uv, GitHub Actions.
- **Docs profile:** `mkdocs` — the full area model, a derived nav, and a strict
  site build inside `task validate`.
- **CI:** GitHub Actions, Sonar on, release on a push to the default branch,
  tagged `v<version>`.

## 1. One entrypoint

`task` is the only entrypoint. Nobody — human, agent, or CI — invokes `uv`,
`mkdocs`, `pnpm`, `npx`, `nx`, `ng` or `kiln` directly.

The developer surface for this repo is exactly:

| Verb | What it does |
| -- | -- |
| `task build` | Build every project with Nx. |
| `task clean` | Remove build outputs, caches, and the rendered docs site. |
| `task docs:build` | Build the MkDocs site into .docs-site/ (or $1 when given). |
| `task docs:generate` | Regenerate the docs' derived regions. |
| `task docs:serve` | Serve the docs site locally with live reload on http://127.0.0.1:8080. |
| `task format` | Format Prettier-formatted files, TOML, YAML and Markdown prose in place. |
| `task kiln:apply` | Re-render the generated files from .rn-forge/kiln/config.toml. Pass --dry-run, or --force \<path> to overwrite a drifted file, after `--`. |
| `task kiln:diff` | Show every generated file that differs from a fresh render, writing nothing. Pass --artifact \<key or path> after `--` to limit it to one. |
| `task kiln:pin` | Move kiln to another ref (tag, branch or SHA) and re-render with it. Pass the ref after `--`. |
| `task lint` | Every lint — Nx projects, Prettier formatting, Markdown, TOML and YAML formatting, kiln's checks, workflow security, dependency vulnerabilities, dependency licences. |
| `task setup` | Install the pnpm workspace and the docs tooling. |
| `task sonar:local` | Run the coverage tests and scan the checked-out branch on SonarCloud, awaiting the quality gate. Needs SONAR_TOKEN and sonar-scanner on PATH; pass --dry-run after -- to print the commands. |
| `task test` | Run every project's tests with Nx. |
| `task test:coverage` | Run every project's tests, writing lcov reports to coverage/. |
| `task typecheck` | Type-check every project through its Angular build. |
| `task validate` | The aggregate gate — lint, typecheck, test, docs build. Any failure fails. |
| `task version` | Print the publishable projects' version, or bump it, write its CHANGELOG.md section and format it (pass -- patch\|minor\|major\|x.y.z). |

The CI surface, `ci:*`, is public only because a workflow step runs it from the
command line, which go-task refuses for an internal task. It is CI's; a
developer has no reason to call it:

| Task | What it does |
| -- | -- |
| `task ci:consumer` | CI only: Install a packed library per peer cell and smoke-test it (-- \<project-root>). |
| `task ci:dist:resolve` | CI only: Resolve the workspace: ranges in a built package's package.json (-- \<dist-dir>). |
| `task ci:dist:verify` | CI only: Check a built package's package.json: no workspace: ranges; name, version, entry point and types present (-- \<dist-dir>). |
| `task ci:docs:site` | CI only: Build Compodoc and Storybook and assemble them under the MkDocs site in .docs-site. |
| `task ci:internal-ranges` | CI only: Check that members depend on each other by workspace:^ or workspace:~. |
| `task ci:release:author` | CI only: Set the git author to the github-actions bot. |
| `task ci:release:finalize` | CI only: Publish the draft GitHub Release for TAG, once npm has the version. |
| `task ci:release:github` | CI only: Create the GitHub Release for TAG as a draft, from the tarballs and kiln-devops notes. |
| `task ci:release:latest` | CI only: Move the rolling latest release to TAG. |
| `task ci:release:publish` | CI only: Publish to npm under DIST_TAG; FIRST_RELEASE_FLAG holds the flag, or nothing. |
| `task ci:release:push` | CI only: Push the tag TAG, and nothing else. |
| `task ci:release:state` | CI only: Write tag, mode=new\|resume\|released, first-release and dist-tag for the version in the pull request to $GITHUB_OUTPUT. |
| `task ci:release:tag` | CI only: Tag HEAD with TAG. |
| `task ci:release:verify` | CI only: Rebuild dist/ from the tagged source, then pack and verify the publishable projects; fails when no tarball was written. |
| `task ci:secret-scan` | CI only: Scan the git history for secrets with the pinned gitleaks (downloads it on first run, so it is not part of lint). |
| `task ci:smoke` | CI only: Pack the publishable projects and verify their tarballs. |
| `task ci:sonar:reports` | CI only: Print the lcov reports found under coverage/ as a reports=\<list> $GITHUB_OUTPUT line, failing when a project wrote none. |
| `task ci:sonar:target` | CI only: Print the Sonar branch argument for this run as a $GITHUB_OUTPUT line. |
| `task ci:test` | CI only: Run Nx targets (-- \<targets>) on the affected projects, or on all of them for a dispatch or a change outside every project. |
| `task ci:test:has-e2e` | CI only: Print whether any project has an e2e target, as a $GITHUB_OUTPUT line. |
| `task ci:test:playwright` | CI only: Install Playwright's browsers and their system dependencies. |
| `task ci:test:playwright-deps` | CI only: Install Playwright's system dependencies, the browsers being cached. |
| `task ci:validate` | CI only: Run the checks that do not run Nx — Markdown, TOML and YAML formatting, kiln's checks, workflow security, the docs build; test-cloud or test-local run the Nx projects. |
| `task ci:verify-release` | CI only: Install what consumers download, the tarballs of the release TAG. |

Every other task is `internal: true`. The root `Taskfile.yml` holds wrappers
only: each of its commands is a `task:` call into a `tasks/*.yml` namespace.
`kiln doctor`'s `task-layout` check enforces both halves of that, and fails if
any gate stops being reachable from `validate`.

**Nx's AI configuration.** Do not run Nx's AI-config generator
(`nx configure-ai-agents`, or an `nx init`/`nx migrate` step that offers it). It
writes a block between `<!-- nx configuration start -->` and
`<!-- nx configuration end -->` into `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md` that tells
readers to run `pnpm nx …`, which this section forbids. If the block is present,
delete the block, markers included.

## 2. One owner per file, or per block

Every path kiln writes or reads has exactly one of these kinds:

| Kind | Owner | Written by | Recorded in `state.json` | Checked by |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| **managed** | kiln | `kiln apply` | the file's SHA-256 | `generated`: drift if the file differs |
| **block** | kiln (the fence); repo (the rest of the file) | `kiln apply` | the body's SHA-256 and the markers | `generated`: drift if the body differs |
| **derived region** | kiln (the fence); repo (the rest of the file) | `kiln docs-generate`, and `kiln new` | nothing | `docs-generate`: stale if regenerating it from the repo's inputs differs |
| **seeded** | repo, after the first write | `kiln apply`, once, when absent | creation only | nothing, including presence |
| **scaffolded** | repo | `kiln new`'s scaffold step, once | its path, in `metadata.scaffolded`, by `kiln new` only | nothing |
| **repo** | repo | never kiln | nothing | the repo's own tasks |
| **input** | repo | the owner, or `kiln config-update` | the hash of its parsed content, as `config_hash` | nothing compares it; `kiln apply` re-renders from it |
| **baseline** | kiln | `kiln apply` | — (it is the record; it never hashes itself) | `generated` reads it |
| **derived data** | kiln | kiln, at run time | nothing | nothing; gitignored |

- A file has one kind, except that a file holding a **block** or **derived
  region** is otherwise scaffolded or repo-owned: `.gitignore`, `AGENTS.md`
  and `mkdocs.yml`.
- **Seeded** and **scaffolded** differ only in who writes them. A seeded file is
  an apply artifact, so a later `kiln apply` recreates it if it is absent and
  never touches it if present. A scaffolded file (`pyproject.toml`,
  `README.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, the bodies of `AGENTS.md` and `mkdocs.yml`, the
  first `libs/` and `apps/`) is written by `kiln new` before its first apply,
  and never again.
- `.tmp/` is the repo's scratch root: disposable, gitignored, removed by
  `task clean`. Tests and tools write their output under it, and nothing kiln
  or the repo keeps lives there.
- Paths kiln neither writes nor reads (`.claude/**`, `.codex/**`, installed
  skills) are not kiln's and have no kind.
- The instruction files are **split by audience.** `README.md` is for people and
  carries no agent directive. `AGENTS.md` is the agent instructions: its body
  is repo-owned and kiln's block is in it, and a tool that adds its own block
  does not own the file. `CLAUDE.md` is `@AGENTS.md` plus what only Claude
  should read, and carries no block.

Managed here: `Taskfile.yml`, `tasks/*.yml`, `.editorconfig`, `.prettierrc`,
`.github/workflows/*.yml`, `.github/actions/setup`, `sonar-project.properties`
and this file. `.rn-forge/kiln/state.json` is generated and committed, and never
hashes itself.

Blocks here: the `# BEGIN rn-forge kiln` region in `.gitignore` and
`.prettierignore`, and the `<!-- BEGIN rn-forge kiln -->` region in `AGENTS.md`.

Derived regions here: the `# BEGIN derived nav` region in `mkdocs.yml`, the
`<!-- BEGIN derived board -->` region in `docs/specs/index.md` and the
`<!-- BEGIN derived scope -->` region in each release page.

Seeded here: `README.md`, `docs/_areas.yml`, `docs/_structure.md`, each area's
`_structure.md` and `index.md`, and `docs/index.md`.

Repo-owned: `pyproject.toml`, `package.json`, `libs/`, `apps/` and `scripts/**`.
After scaffolding, doctor ignores their content and the content and presence of
seeded files. Repository validation tasks may check these independently. Only
managed files and fenced blocks remain kiln's responsibility.

To change a managed file, change `.rn-forge/kiln/config.toml` and run
`kiln apply`. To change what kiln renders, change kiln's templates: every
shipped archetype × flag cell is rendered, validated, and approved by the owner
before the change is done.

## 3. The dependency set

A `node-lib` repository declares no rn-forge library: its root `pyproject.toml`
carries only kiln's tooling and the docs group, and its code dependencies are
pnpm's.

kiln is not a dependency. `[kiln] ref` in `config.toml` pins it, and `task` runs
it with `uvx` in its own environment (kiln ADR-0006). A repository's lock holds
none of kiln's dependencies, and kiln's pykit pins never constrain the
repository's.

To move the pin to another ref (a tag, a branch or a SHA, higher or lower), run
`task kiln:pin -- <ref>`. It checks that the ref resolves, sets `[kiln] ref`,
and re-renders with the kiln at that ref, so the move is one reviewable diff. Do
not edit the ref by hand: `task kiln:apply` would then run the old kiln.

## 4. The import boundary

A `node-lib` repository has no `.importlinter`. The boundaries between its
projects are the repository's own, in the `@nx/enforce-module-boundaries` rule
of `eslint.config.mjs`, and `task lint` runs them.

## 5. What CI checks, and what it does not

CI runs the pinned kiln read-only: it never runs `kiln apply` and never writes a
generated file. `task validate` runs `kiln doctor` on every run;
`kiln doctor --full` runs where the workflow asks, through `lint` with the
`KILN_DOCTOR_FULL` task variable set. `[ci] doctor_full` chooses where: pushes
to the default branch and dispatch by default, or every run. Branch protection
requires `ci-ok` and nothing else.

`task validate` proves: the archetype's dependency set is present, allowed and
pinned; the task layout and validate gate are intact; no workflow step invokes a
wrapped tool; the docs tree matches `docs/_areas.yml`; the derived nav is
current; no link or anchor is broken; **every managed file and block still
hashes to the value committed in `.rn-forge/kiln/state.json`**; the tests pass;
and the docs site builds `--strict`.

## 6. What `kiln doctor --full` adds

Exactly one question `kiln doctor` cannot ask without `--full`: whether a newer
kiln, or an edited config, would now render something different from what is
committed. kiln is modules under one contract — each owns its config section,
its `artifacts()` and its `checks()` — and `kiln doctor` collects every module's
findings into one report. Full verification checks managed artifacts against a
fresh render; it does not compare repository-owned files with scaffold defaults.

## 7. The state baseline

`.rn-forge/kiln/state.json` is generated and committed. It holds, per artifact,
the repo-relative path, the kind, and a SHA-256 — of the whole file for managed
artifacts, of the body for blocks — plus the exact fence markers for blocks, and
a creation record for seeded files, whose presence is not enforced. It records
`kiln_version` and `config_hash` in its metadata, and it never contains an entry
for itself. `scaffolded` lists the paths `kiln new` wrote that no artifact owns;
nothing checks them.

`kiln doctor`'s `generated` check reads it without rendering anything.

## 8. Configuration

`.rn-forge/kiln/config.toml` is the one committed input. Kiln owns only its
`.rn-forge/kiln/` namespace and ignores sibling directories. Configuration is
resolved once: `kiln new --config <path|git-url[@ref]>` deep-merges kiln
defaults, each source layer and flags — lists replace — and records a `git+`
source in a `[source]` table; a local file is read and not recorded.
`kiln apply` and `kiln doctor` read only the committed file.
`kiln config update` re-resolves the source with the running kiln,
`kiln config upgrade` with a newer one; each changes nothing without `--apply`,
and keeps a key edited here as a repo override.

## CI checks

Switch a configured check in `[ci.checks]`; see the CI architecture page for the
model.

| Check | Verb | Switch and key |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Markdown, TOML and YAML formatting | `task lint` | S |
| `kiln doctor` | `task lint` | S; `--full` per `[ci] doctor_full`, default `default-branch` |
| zizmor, actionlint | `task lint` | S |
| `pnpm-audit` | `task node:lint:audit` | S |
| Nx lint, typecheck, test, build | `task node:*`, `task ci:test` | S |
| Docs strict build | `task docs:build` | D: `[docs] profile = "mkdocs"` |
| `dependency-review` | action | S |
| Sonar | `sonar` job | C: `[ci] sonar`, default `true` |
| Release | `release` job | C: `[ci] release`, default `tag-exists`; `pypi` for `python-lib`; `nx-dispatch` for `node-lib`; `none` |
| `verify-release` | `task ci:verify-release` | D: a release mode other than `none` |
| Docs deploy | `docs` job | D: `[docs] profile = "mkdocs"` |
| Package tarballs | `task ci:smoke` | S |
| `ci-ok` | none | S |
| `licenses` | `task node:lint:licenses` | C: `[ci.checks] licenses`, default `true`; a table sets `deny` and `ignore` |
| `secret-scan` | `task ci:secret-scan` | C: `[ci.checks] secret-scan`, default `true` |
| `internal-ranges` | `task ci:internal-ranges` | D: two or more workspace members |
| `umbrella-release` | `task ci:release:umbrella` | C: `[ci.checks] umbrella-release`, default `false` |
| `scorecard` | none | C: `[ci.checks] scorecard`, default `false`; public repositories only |

A repository-owned workflow is allowed only for a scheduled or non-gating run;
it keeps its own action pins current through Dependabot, which ignores the
actions kiln pins.

## 9. What a node-lib repository declares

kiln renders the CI; the repository declares what that CI runs. None of this is
generated after `kiln new`, and `kiln doctor` reads none of it.

**In `nx.json`.** `kiln new` writes these once; keep them.

- `release`: `projects` holds `tag:publishable`, `version.preVersionCommand`
  builds those projects (and runs `patch-package-exports` for any that declare
  it), and `changelog.workspaceChangelog.createRelease` is `false`.
- `targetDefaults.pack` depends on `build` and packs `dist/<project>` into
  `dist/tarballs/`. `targetDefaults.verify-dist` depends on `pack`, is not
  cached, and checks the packed manifest.

Add `nxCloudId` when the repository moves to Nx Cloud.

**In each publishable project's `project.json`.** The tag `publishable`, and the
targets `"pack": {}` and `"verify-dist": {}`, which take their commands from
`targetDefaults`. The project generator also adds the project's name to
`release.projects`, and it can stay there. Without the tag, `task version` finds
no publishable project and a release fails in its state step, before anything is
pushed. With the tag but without `pack`, a release fails in its verify step,
before anything is pushed, with `No tarball in dist/tarballs`. Until npm
publishing is set up, add `"dryRun": true` to the `nx-release-publish` options:
the project generator does not write it, and without it the release's Publish
step publishes to npm.

**Releasing.** A release follows a version bump made in a pull request: run
`task version -- <patch|minor|major|x.y.z>` (`nx release version`, no commit or
tag), commit the changed `package.json` files and the new `CHANGELOG.md`
section, and merge. `task version` with no argument prints the version. On the
push to the default branch, `release` tags `v<version>`, publishes to npm under
the dist-tag the version names (`latest` for `x.y.z`, the prerelease identifier
for `x.y.z-<id>.<n>`), and publishes the GitHub Release last. CI never commits.
A version whose GitHub Release is published is skipped.

**For a publishable library's consumer check.** Add `"verify-consumer": {}` to
its `project.json`, which takes its command from `targetDefaults`, and declare
the peer matrix under `workspace-ci.consumer` in its `package.json`: the
`dependencies` and `preload` every cell shares, the `cells` (each with its own),
and an optional `hook`. `task ci:consumer` installs the packed tarball into one
fixture per cell and imports every entry point. A hook is one `.mjs` file that
runs inside the fixture, so its bare imports resolve to the installed tarball
and the cell's dependencies; it imports no sibling file. `dist-resolve` keeps
the matrix out of the published manifest. The
[example](https://github.com/rn-forge/kiln/blob/main/docs/specs/epics/E9-node-archetypes/F9.4-node-helpers-in-kiln-devops.md#s945-kiln-devops-consumer-smoke-tests-a-packed-library-across-its-peer-matrix)
shows the shape.

**Targets CI runs.** `lint`, `test` (writing lcov under `coverage/`), `build`
and `e2e` (`e2e-ci` on Nx Cloud), on the affected projects. Optional, declared
per project: `verify-consumer` (a check that runs against the packed tarballs;
`package`, the release and `verify-release` run it wherever it is declared),
`patch-package-exports`, and, for the Pages site, `compodoc` (output
`dist/compodoc/<project>`) and `build-storybook` (output
`dist/storybook/<project>`), published under `api/` and `storybook/`.

**Variables and secrets.**

| Name | Kind | Used by | Meaning |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `USE_NX_CLOUD` | variable | `ci.yml` | `true` runs `test-cloud` on Nx Cloud agents; anything else runs `test-local`. A dispatch's `use-nx-cloud` input decides instead |
| `NX_CLOUD_AGENTS` | variable | `test-cloud` | agent count; optional, default 3 |
| `NX_CLOUD_ACCESS_TOKEN` | secret | `test-cloud` | the Nx Cloud access token |
| `SONAR_TOKEN` | secret | `sonar` | the SonarCloud token |
| `RELEASE_APP_CLIENT_ID` | variable | `release` | the release GitHub App's client ID |
| `RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` | secret | `release` | the release GitHub App's private key |

**Once per repository.**

- GitHub Pages: Settings, Pages, Source: GitHub Actions. The `docs` job deploys
  from `main`.
- Branch protection or a ruleset on `main` requires the `ci-ok` check and
  nothing else.
- The release pushes its tag as a GitHub App with Contents read and write.
  Install it on the repository and make it an `Always` bypass actor on any
  ruleset that blocks direct pushes. Use no deploy key or personal access
  token.

**Action pins.** The `uses:` SHAs in generated files are kiln's. They move when
kiln's `cicd/pins.toml` changes and the repository moves `[kiln] ref` and runs
`kiln apply`. Editing one is drift: `kiln doctor` fails, `kiln apply` refuses,
and `kiln apply --force <path>` restores kiln's SHA, keeping a backup under
`.rn-forge/kiln/backups`. Dependabot's `npm` and `uv` pull requests edit
`package.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml` and `pyproject.toml`, which kiln does not
manage, so they are not drift. The generated `dependabot.yml` has no
`github-actions` block for generated workflows, for the same reason.
